title: Songo Mnara
summary: Songo Mnara is a Swahili stone town on a small island in the Kilwa archipelago, off southern Tanzania, listed by UNESCO with Kilwa Kisiwani. UNESCO records five mosques, a palace complex and some thirty-three dwellings of coral stone and wood; Rice University researchers count more than 40 large room blocks. Rice says it took part in Indian Ocean commerce in the 15th and 16th centuries and was quickly abandoned.

uncertainty.note: Rice University: central participant in Indian Ocean commerce during the 15th and 16th centuries. UNESCO dates Kilwa and Songo Mnara trade prosperity particularly to the 13th-16th centuries. The span follows Rice.

as_recorded.value: Songo Mnara was a central participant in Indian Ocean commerce during the 15th and 16th centuries

where.modern_name: Songo Mnara, Kilwa District, Lindi Region, Tanzania
where.historical_name: Songo Mnara, Swahili town in the Kilwa archipelago

importance.justification: UNESCO says Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara bear exceptional testimony to Swahili coastal culture, the Islamisation of East Africa and Indian Ocean trade.

reviewer_note: No model: no height-plus-plan dimension for a single building was sourced. Counts conflict and are quoted per source: UNESCO five mosques, a palace complex and some thirty-three domestic dwellings; Rice "more than 40 large domestic room blocks, five mosques". Dates: Rice 15th-16th century; UNESCO gives the 13th-16th centuries for the two ports together; the span follows Rice. The pin is UNESCO's second geolocation for entry 144 (the first is Kilwa Kisiwani).
